title: Customs Classification, Tariff and Rules of Interpretation

content.overview: Imported or exported goods are classified in the Customs Tariff, read with the General Rules for the Interpretation of the tariff. Classification decides the rate. It does not decide valuation or exemption. A heading is chosen by terms, section and chapter notes, and then by the interpretation rules. The tariff text and notes prevail over trade description.
content.glance: Customs Classification, Tariff and Rules of Interpretation. Complete Tax treatise with statutory deconstruction, examples, verified authorities, forum analysis and chamber drafting.
content.study: Identify the goods, read the notes, apply the interpretation rule, and only then read the rate.

sections.heading: Procedural Roadmap, Forum and Limitation Checkpoints
sections.body:

Transition and current law: identify the tax period, charging statute, commencement date, amendment or notification in force, taxable event, jurisdictional notice and statutory appeal or writ route; use the Income-tax Act, 1961 only as historical transition/concordance where the 2025 Act applies

cases.name: Govind Saran Ganga Saran v. Commissioner of Sales Tax
cases.facts: The Court examined the components of a valid charging provision.
cases.issue: What must a tax levy clearly identify to be valid?
cases.ratioDecidendi: A valid levy ordinarily identifies the taxable event, person liable, rate and measure or value of the tax.
cases.holding: The Court treated these components as essential to a charging scheme.
cases.relevance: Use for charge, levy and statutory certainty.

cases.name: Union of India v. Azadi Bachao Andolan
cases.facts: The Court considered treaty benefits, circulars and tax avoidance arguments.
cases.issue: How should a valid tax treaty and administrative circular operate?
cases.ratioDecidendi: A treaty and valid administrative practice must be respected unless displaced by law; legitimate tax planning is not automatically evasion.
cases.holding: The Court upheld the challenged treaty approach in the circumstances.
cases.relevance: Use for statutory interpretation, treaties and tax planning.

cases.name: Union of India v. Mohit Minerals Pvt. Ltd.
cases.facts: The case concerned GST levy and the legal effect of a Council recommendation.
cases.issue: What is the constitutional and statutory force of GST Council recommendations?
cases.ratioDecidendi: GST Council recommendations have persuasive value within the constitutional design but are not automatically binding as primary legislation without statutory implementation.
cases.holding: The Court interpreted the federal GST framework accordingly.
cases.relevance: Use for GST levy, delegated action and constitutional federalism.

I. ISSUE AND JURISDICTION
Whether Customs Classification, Tariff and Rules of Interpretation applies to the stated facts and whether the chosen forum and remedy are maintainable.

II. GOVERNING RULE
Customs Classification, Tariff and Rules of Interpretation is governed by Income-tax Act, 2025; Income-tax Rules, 2026; CGST Act, 2017; IGST Act, 2017; applicable SGST Acts; and Customs Act, 1962, together with current rules, notifications and circulars. identify the tax period, charging statute, commencement date, amendment or notification in force, taxable event, jurisdictional notice and statutory appeal or writ route; use the Income-tax Act, 1961 only as historical transition/concordance where the 2025 Act applies.

III. INGREDIENT APPLICATION
Identify each condition, connect it to the evidence and answer the principal exception or defence. Apply BSA s. 63 to digital records where relevant and state the initial burden precisely.

IV. CONCLUSION
Grant, refuse or modify the relief only to the extent authorised by the governing law and proved record.

enhancement.definition: Imported or exported goods are classified in the Customs Tariff, read with the General Rules for the Interpretation of the tariff. Classification decides the rate. It does not decide valuation or exemption. A heading is chosen by terms, section and chapter notes, and then by the interpretation rules.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: The tariff text and notes prevail over trade description.
enhancement.statutoryFramework: Customs Tariff Act, 1975; General Rules for Interpretation.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: The Rules of Interpretation start with heading terms and legal notes. A specific heading prevails over a general one. Essential character is used for mixtures and composite goods where the rule applies. The last rule classifies under the heading to which the goods are most akin. A commercial name is evidence of identity, not a heading.
examples: A machine is described by its use, but a tariff note places it in a specific heading.
The more specific heading is preferred.
